name: The eight bonds (aṣṭa-pāśa)
description: The eight fetters beginning with disgust, whose destruction is liberation while living (Dīpikā on YH 1.86); the guru burns the disciple's bonds at initiation (PKS 1.36).
antidotes: knowledge of the cakra-code through the guru
notes: Only 'beginning with disgust' is checked; the full list is the common Kaula one (Kulārṇava), recalled from memory.

name: The six inner enemies (kāma, krodha, lobha, moha, mada, mātsarya)
description: Desire, anger, greed, delusion, pride and envy are to be avoided (PKS 1.19); in the Bhāvanā Upaniṣad they, with merit and demerit, are the eight Mothers (Brāhmī and the others) of the first enclosure — to be recognized as powers of the Goddess.

name: Breach of the samaya
description: Breaking the initiate's observances; for those without lineage and proud of mere knowledge, through this breach the mantra's rays turn against them (YH 2.81).

equivalents.note: the Śrīvidyā statement of the Mantramārga fault of breaking initiatory rules

name: Knowledge without lineage (pride of book-learning)
description: Knowledge gained from books without the succession of teachers breeds pride and harm (YH 2.81); the flow of the mind to the meaning comes only by the guru's grace (Setubandha).

name: Recitation without knowing the meaning
description: Uttering the mantra without its meaning bears no fruit, like oblation on ash; it may even harm (VR 54-56).

name: Making the secret public (prākaṭya)
description: Exposure of the secret worship leads to hell (PKS 1.12); the Kaula Upaniṣad forbids telling one's secret except to a disciple; Bhāskararāya calls non-exposure the chief of Kaula conducts.

name: Outward-facing mind (bahirmukhatā)
description: The Goddess is 'very hard to reach for those turned outward' (LSN 162).

name: Ignorance as inner darkness
description: The Goddess is the sun-city for the inner darkness of the ignorant (SL 3); 'cit' is the fire-pit because it opposes the darkness that is ignorance (Bhāskararāya on LSN name 4).

name: Censure of other schools
description: Censuring any school is forbidden (PKS 1.14; Kaula Upaniṣad): the schools are valid for their own qualified followers, and censure makes them doubt their own way without qualifying them for the Kaula (Bhāskararāya).

name: Doubt
description: Worship of one guru is to be without doubt (PKS 1.20); all success comes through tradition and faith (PKS 1.9-10).

name: Pursuit of particular powers
description: The sixty-four tantras, each bent on producing its own particular powers, beguiled the world; the Goddess's tantra alone accomplishes all the aims of life (SL 31); the gods obtained powers only by waiting at her gate (SL 93).
